extracted.intended_audience: agency staff, administrative law practitioners, and agency rulemakers
extracted.subtask_description: Lists the types of administrative proceedings reported for many federal agencies and provides an illustrative President's Conference rule for appeals from intermediate agency decisions (notice of appeal, effect of exceptions, replies, content, enlargement of time, and filing periods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Securities and Exchange Commission — Types of proceedings reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Stop orders (SA), Rev. or susp. of broker-dealer, [member] (SEA), Suspension or withdrawal of registration (SEA), Approval of sales, acquisitions, exemptions, or reorganization plan (PUHCA), Exemption or other relief (ICA), IAA registration, Disbarment (SA & SEA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed proceeding is referenced to the applicable U.S.C. citations (examples in text: 15 USC 77h(d); 15 USC 78o(b); 15 USC 78s(a),78x1; PUHCA citations; ICA citations). The entry is part of a table summarizing types of proceedings reported by the agencies and their statutory bases; totals are tabulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subversive Activities Control Board — Types of proceedings reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings involving communist action, front, infiltrated organizations (statutory reference visible: 50 USC 792j, 792a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the 'Types of Proceedings Reported by the Agencies' table with statutory citations for classification and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treasury Department / Coast Guard — Types of proceedings reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension or revocation of marine licenses (statutory citations: 46 USC 239, 239b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as an agency-specific category in the table of reported proceedings; used to classify enforcement/adjudicatory actions for reporting purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agriculture Department — Types of proceedings reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing order contests (AMA), CEA and P&S cease and desist orders, P&S license revocation or suspension and cease and desist orders, P&S rate determinations, PACA license denial, CEA suspension or revocation of registration and suspension of trading privileges, PACA lie. susp. or rev. (statutory citations include 7 USC provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table lists these items with statutory references (e.g. 7 USC 608c(15)(A), 7 USC 13a, 193, 211, 7 USC 204,205,213,218d, etc.). These categories indicate which kinds of agency actions are counted/reported in the appendix totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil Aeronautics (Board) — Types of proceedings reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Route licensing (49 USC 481), foreign permits (49 USC 482), adequacy of service (49 USC 484), mail rates (49 USC 486).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency-specific proceedings are listed with citations to relevant U.S. Code sections for classification in the reporting tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Power Commission — Types of proceedings reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural Gas Act and Federal Power Act related proceedings: investigations, suspensions, cost and rate matters, extension of facilities, export/import applications, certificates under NGA sections (e.g., 15 USC references such as 717c, 717d(a), 717f(a), 717b), water power construction licenses (16 USC 797), FPA rate determinations and related actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A detailed list of FPC/NGA/FPA categories with statutory citations. Used to classify and tally agency adjudications and regulatory proceedings in the appendix tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food and Drug Administration — Types of proceedings reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of new drug application (statutory reference: 21 USC 355(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Health, Education, and Welfare / FDA entries in the table of reported agency proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Security Administration — Types of proceedings reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals from benefits rights determinations (statutory reference: 42 USC 405).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the agency-by-agency table indicating the kinds of proceedings counted for statistical/reporting purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior Department — Bureau of Land Management types reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Government contests (43 USC 120), private contests (43 USC 1201, 30 USC 527(c)), placer mining orders (30 USC 62), appeals from Range Managers' decisions (43 USC 315h), FRC enforcement proceedings (43 USC 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BLM-specific categories appear in the table with citations; used for reporting the agency's adjudicatory output/totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bureau of Indian Affairs — Types of proceedings reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Indian probate and related proceedings (statutory references indicated: 25 USC ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the agencies table (footnotes referenced); serves as a classification for reporting BIA adjudicatory actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types-of-proceedings reporting practice (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are tabulated with statutory categories and totals for the types of proceedings they report (the appendix contains repeated tables listing agency-by-agency categories and U.S.C. citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appendix's tables are used as the standard for what proceedings are counted and how they are categorized across federal agencies; the tables include footnotes, totals, and cross-references to statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential Conference Illustrative Rule — Notice of Appeal (a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of Appeal — 'Any party may ... an initial or recommended decision ... or from a tentative decision ... twenty days after service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative rule language in the appendix: parties must file a notice of appeal/exceptions within the specified period (the text shows 'twenty days after service' as the illustrative filing period). This functions as a model procedural deadline for appeals from intermediate decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential Conference Illustrative Rule — Effect of Exceptions (c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of Exceptions — 'The effectiveness of the intermediate decision shall be stayed if any party files a notice of appeal and exceptions within the times specified above or if the agency upon notice to the parties undertakes to review the decision. Otherwise, the intermediate decision shall become the final decision of the agency.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision sets the effect of filing exceptions/appeals (automatic stay of the intermediate decision if timely exceptions/appeals are filed or agency review is undertaken). It is an explicit procedural rule to govern interim decision status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential Conference Illustrative Rule — Replies (d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies — 'Within ten days after service of exceptions, any opposing party may file a reply to such exceptions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model timeline for responsive filings following exceptions; it defines the short reply period (ten days) for opposing parties to respond to exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential Conference Illustrative Rule — Content of Exceptions (e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content — 'Exceptions shall identify specifically the findings, conclusions, or proposed action to which objection is made, and shall be supported by concise argument and by specific page references to the parts of the record and the legal and other authorities relied upon.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prescribes drafting standards for exceptions: specificity (identify findings/conclusions/proposed action), concise argumentation, and precise citation to record pages and legal authorities. It is both a procedural and a quality/content standard for filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential Conference Illustrative Rule — Enlargement of Time (f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enlargement of Time — 'The time periods prescribed by this rule may be extended by the agency for good cause.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the standard by which agencies may grant extensions of the filing deadlines in the illustrative rule — 'good cause' is the governing standard for enlargement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix filing-periods table (agency-specific deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: A tabulated list showing 'Days after decision in which to file' (columns include Notice of Exceptions, Replies, Appeals, etc.) with agency-specific numbers (examples in table: many agencies indicated with 10, 20, 30 days or other periods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table functions as a reference of model or actual filing periods for different agencies; footnotes and cross-references (e.g., CFR citations) explain exceptions and maximums (e.g., '10 CFR 2.751-.752', other notes about extensions or special rules). Use the table as authoritative source for agency filing deadlines and any special procedural caveats noted in footnotes.
